 Honda reveals the latest ADV in the range, with adventure looks and CBT friendly credentials
 By Tommy Begley 
 Follow MCN on Google 
 Add MCN as a preferred source on Google to see more of our latest content
 Published: Yesterday 15:30 
 Previous Slide ◀ 
 Next Slide ▶ 
 Honda ADV125 in grey wizzing past some shipping containers 
 1 of 5 
 Honda have just unveiled the latest member of the ADV family, the A1-friendly twist-and-go ADV125.
 The Japanese manufacturer describes the new scooter as ‘an exclusive urban explorer’, with design cues taken from the sports utility vehicle (SUV) market and say it follows on from the success of the X-ADV750 released in 2017 and the A2 compliant ADV350 released in 2022.
 The CBT-friendly bike produces just over 12bhp at 8750rpm using the same Euro 5+ engine found in the ever-popular PCX125 , but producing 3lb.ft more torque at 11.7lb.ft at 6500rpm.
 Named the eSP+ engine, it comes equipped with economic ‘stop-start’ technology and Honda selectable torque control (HSTC), which helps to stop wheelspin in poor conditions, and can be switched off if desired.
 The new scooter boasts an impressive 134.4mpg and 239 miles from its 8.1-litre tank under test conditions. This frugality is said to be achieved, in part, by the firm’s low-friction technologies like its offset cylinder, ‘spiny’ cast-iron cylinder sleeve and hydraulic cam chain tensioner, all of which help to reduce tension in the piston ring, reduce vibrations, thus improving fuel economy.
 The bike’s oil jets are the same as those used in Honda’s CRF450R competition MX bike, which are built into the crankcase to help with consistent and efficient engine cooling. Paired with a new, larger 28mm throttle body they are suggested to optimise fuel burning velocity and aid cooling.
 Related: Check out MCN’s guide to the best urban motorcycle boots 
 The chassis is said by Honda to deliver ‘genuine rough-road capabilities’ with its duplex steel cradle tubular underbone frame for strength and long-travel Showa suspension with 116mm front travel and external reservoir-donned rear shocks offering 103mm of travel.
 The 14in front and 13in rear wheels with blocky, tubeless Pirelli Tourance tyres complete the look. Wavy 240mm front and 220mm rear brake discs handle the stopping duties and the cast wheels and 165mm ground clearance suggest more on-road application.
 Related: Read MCN’s guide to the best learner-legal motorcycles 
 With an accessible 780mm seat height, upright riding position and adjustable by 75mm windscreen, the ADV125 is said to offer comfort for most riders come rain or shine. It should also be fairly nimble, even at slow city speeds, with a kerb weight of 133kg and 1324mm wheelbase.
 Creature comforts one would expect on a scooter remain, like 29 litres of under-seat storage, a two-litre glove box, a USB-C charging socket and even smart key operation for ignition. You can also add a 40-litre top box if you need to carry a lot. Besides the box, optional extras include factory-fitted heated grips and a security buzzer.
 The smart key can be set to ‘answer back’ too, which sets off the scooter’s buzzer and indicators should you misplace it.
 The 5in TFT display works with Honda’s Roadsync app to provide music control, sat-nav, texts and more from your phone.
 The MCN take
 Simultaneously hitting the CBT-friendly and adventure bike craze should make the ADV125 very popular on paper. It might not really be suited to rough adventuring but is likely to be a hit on the city streets and country lanes.
